content: Poland Spring is a brand of bottled water that is produced by a subsidiary of Nestlé. The company was originally established in 1845 by Hiram Ricker. Contrary to what many people believe, not all Poland Spring water originates from the town of Poland, Maine. Instead, the water is sourced from multiple locations across the state of Maine. These sources include Poland Spring in Poland, Maine; Clear Spring in Hollis; Evergreen Spring in Fryeburg; Spruce Spring in Pierce Pond Township; Garden Spring in Poland, Maine; and White Cedar Spring in Dallas Plantation, Maine. Poland Spring is currently the best-selling spring water brand in the United States. The history of the brand dates back to the late 18th century. In 1794, Jabez Ricker purchased land in Maine. Shortly after, travelers began stopping at his property, requesting meals. This led him to open an inn called the Mansion House in 1797. By 1844, Jabez’s grandson, Hiram Ricker, began drinking large quantities of water from the spring on the property. He became convinced that the water had cured his chronic dyspepsia. At the time, it was a popular trend to take the waters as a remedy for various illnesses. This belief, combined with the growing reputation of the spring water, increased the inn’s popularity. The Ricker family began bottling the water, and the inn eventually expanded into a prominent resort during the late 19th and early 20th centuries. However, the Ricker family lost control of the company during the 1930s. A resort still operates on the original site today. In 1901, Maine’s Bureau of Industrial and Labor Statistics reported that there were 81 mineral springs in the state, 23 of which were used for commercial bottling. At the time, total sales from these springs amounted to $400,000, with Poland Spring accounting for $200,000 of that figure. Today, Poland Spring primarily sells its water in portable plastic bottles of various sizes, including 8 oz, 12 oz, 20 oz, 500 mL, 700 mL, 1 L, and 1.5 L. Larger 5-gallon bottles are also available for use in office or home water dispensers. Additionally, smaller 1-gallon and 2.5-gallon bottles are sold in supermarkets and offered for home delivery in the Northeastern United States. Poland Spring also produces less common varieties of water, such as sparkling water and flavored options like lemon and lime, as well as distilled water. All Poland Spring products are packaged in plastic bottles for reasons of safety and cost efficiency. The company also manufactures the Aquapod line of products. In the summer of 2005, Poland Spring made changes to its packaging. The cap color of its 1-gallon bottles was changed from dark green to clear, and the safety seal was replaced with a stronger twist-off mechanism. This change was implemented to reduce the risk of taste complaints and to save on material costs. In September 2007, Poland Spring introduced a new, lighter bottle design to reduce waste and improve sustainability. Poland Spring and its parent company, Nestlé, have faced criticism and opposition from several towns in Maine due to their business practices. For example, in Fryeburg, Maine, Poland Spring purchases 110 million gallons of water annually from the Fryeburg Water Company, which also supplies water to the town itself. Concerns arose in Fryeburg about the volume of water being sold to Poland Spring. In 2004, the town experienced a temporary water shortage due to a pump failure, but Poland Spring’s operations were unaffected. A local advocacy group, H₂O for ME, has proposed implementing a tax on water extracted for commercial purposes. However, Poland Spring has argued that such a tax would lead to the company’s bankruptcy. Wilfong has also suggested revising laws to impose limits on the amount of groundwater that landowners can extract from their property.
